note_tweet.text:
When will there be a Trial??

Nearly three years. Sixteen court appearances. Still no trial.

Former Louisiana High School teacher Tatum Hatch was accused in December 2023 of an inappropriate relationship with a 15-year-old student. Almost three years later, the criminal case remains unresolved.

According to the latest report, Hatch appeared before Judge Jeffery Joyce on October 13, 2026, for her 16th court appearance. The next hearing is scheduled for December 7, just before the third anniversary of the original complaint.

Hatch faces charges of computer-aided solicitation of a minor for sexual purposes, sexual battery, and indecent behavior with juveniles. She has pleaded not guilty.

Investigators reported that the student provided sexually explicit Instagram messages allegedly exchanged with Hatch. The student also alleged sexual contact inside her vehicle.

Hatch was arrested January 3, 2024, and released on bond the following day. Since then, the case has moved through repeated hearings, status conferences, and postponed trial dates. A trial scheduled for July 28, 2025, did not take place.

The available information does not fully explain why the case has taken this long.

She is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. But these are serious allegations involving a child, and nearly three years later, there is still no verdict.

Another court date is on the calendar. When will there be a trial?
